append.text: **Ps 13:6 *consílium ínopis confudístis* (the evildoers, plural, between two verses naming the Lord in the third person):** the Ps 10:2 remedy used again — ***vós envergonhastes*** (the subject named); the blind reader heard it as said to the evildoers, not to God. The remedy holds twice now.

**Ps 13:1b *in stúdiis suis* (ἐν ἐπιτηδεύμασιν, the row's named test) → *nos seus feitos*** (*tornaram-se abomináveis nos seus feitos*): the Latinist passed it twice, the blind reader heard it without remark. Both places of the word (grep) now say *feitos* — of God in 9:12, of the wicked in 13:1b; ready to settle.

**Ps 13:6 *consílium ínopis* → *o conselho do indigente***, kept under this row: **listed as unknown by the blind reader for the third time** (Ps 11 twice, Ps 13 once). Heard otherwise rightly (the next colon's *a sua esperança* taken as his). The evidence against *indigente* is now three readings of three; if it is to change, *desvalido* (MS1932 in Ps 11) is the candidate that keeps *pobre* for pauper.

**Ps 13:7 *cum avérterit Dóminus captivitátem plebis suæ* → *quando o Senhor afastar o cativeiro do seu povo*:** draft 1 had this row's *desviar*; the stylist found *desviar o cativeiro* not Portuguese and the blind reader could not tell whether the captivity was present or threatened. *Afastar* (the stylist's) taken there — it shares a verb with *amovére / repéllere* (row *amovére*), which never meet *captivitátem*. *Desviar* stays right with a face (12:1) or anger (77:38, 105:24 *ut avérteret iram*). **84:2 *avertísti captivitátem Jacob* should follow Ps 13 (*afastastes o cativeiro de Jacó*). The twin 52:7 has *convérterit* (row *convértere*) and should differ.**

**Ps 13:3a *Omnes declinavérunt* (absolute; = 52:4 = Rom 3:12) → *Todos se desviaram*:** without *a*, and next to *juntos* (*simul*), *se apartaram* risks 'they parted from one another'; the reflexive *desviar-se* is not avértere's transitive *desviar*. The blind reader heard 'turned from the good'. Absolute *declinavérunt* elsewhere (20:12, 54:4 *in me*, 101:12 of days like a shadow) is another build; 77:57 *avertérunt se* will also be *se desviaram* — two Latin verbs share a form there.

**Ps 13:6 the active with men as subject, *consílium ínopis confudístis* → *vós envergonhastes o conselho do indigente*:** D15's verb holds in the active; the Latinist passed it twice, the blind reader heard 'put to shame' without remark (he heard *conselho* as advice given).
Ps 13:4 *qui dévorant plebem meam* → *os que devoram o meu povo*; 13:7 *captivitátem plebis suæ* → *o cativeiro do seu povo* — applied, as this row named; no reader remarked. 52:5, 52:7 copy them.

Ps 13:5 *illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor* → *ali tremeram de temor, onde não havia temor* (the noun twice, as the Latin; = 52:6b); *tremer de medo* (MS1932) is the option. 13:3d *timor Dei* → *temor de Deus*.

**Ps 13:4 *Nonne cognóscent omnes* (no object) → *Não hão de saber todos*:** *conhecer* wants an object; collocation governs, as 118:152. The twin 52:5 *Nonne scient* (the same Greek γνώσονται) should copy it. 13:3d *viam pacis non cognovérunt* (with an object) → *não conheceram o caminho da paz*.

**Ps 13:2 *aut requírens Deum* (ἐκζητῶν, = 52:3b, = Rom 3:11) → *ou quem procure a Deus*:** requírere merged into this row's verb again, on the Greek, as at 118:145; *busque* (MS1932, DM1962) is the option. 9:13 *requírens sánguinem* (God, of blood) stays *pedir contas*.
Ps 13:1b, 13:3a *abominábiles facti sunt … inútiles facti sunt* → *tornaram-se abomináveis … se tornaram inúteis* (a state come upon them; the repetition kept); = 52:2, 52:4.
Ps 13:3a *simul inútiles facti sunt* → *juntos se tornaram inúteis*: *simul* shares *juntos* (see the new row *simul*); 48:3 *simul in unum* must decide locally.

terms: | insípiens / insipiéntia | insensato / insensatez | open | Ps 13:1a (= 52:1) *Disse o insensato no seu coração: * Não há Deus* — ἄφρων; MS1932 in Ps 13 and DM1962. 14 lines (grep): the adjective 48:11 and 91:7 stand beside *stultus*, so it must stay apart from *tolo / estulto*; 73:18 *pópulus insípiens*, 75:5 *insipiéntes corde*, 93:8 *Intellégite, insipiéntes*; the noun 21:3, 37:6, 38:9, 68:6. Passed the Latinist twice; no reader remarked. Options *néscio* (MS1932 in Ps 52), *tolo* |

| prospícere | olhar (*O Senhor olhou do céu para os filhos dos homens*) | open | Ps 13:2 (= 52:3 with *Deus*). L&S 'to look forward, into the distance, look out'; διέκυψεν. Draft 1 had *olhou do céu sobre* for *super*; the stylist heard a calque and the preposition yields (D2). Other places 36:13 *próspicit* (foresees), 84:12 *justítia de cælo prospéxit*, 101:20 *prospéxit de excélso* (grep) — the *pro-* is not heard; must stay apart from respícere (*estar voltado para*, *olhai*) and aspícere (*Olhai para mim*). Option *se debruçou do céu sobre* (the Greek's image) |

| contrítio | ruína (*Ruína e infelicidade nos seus caminhos*) | open | Ps 13:3d (= Rom 3:16; σύντριμμα); only singular here — 59:4, 146:3 *contritiónes* (breaches, wounds) will want another word. The noun of contérere → quebrar, but *quebranto* is the evil eye in Brazil. Cost: *ruína* is also a Latin word of the psalter (105:29, 109:6, 143:14). Passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'they cause ruin' first. Options *destruição* (DRB; proposed for intéritus), *aflição* (MS1932) |
| infelícitas | infelicidade | working | Ps 13:3d only (grep); ταλαιπωρία; the cognate, current |

| simul | juntos | open | Ps 13:3a (= 52:4) *juntos se tornaram inúteis* (DRB *together*); 15 lines (grep): 30:14, 87:18 *together*; 48:11 *simul insípiens, et stultus* is 'alike'; **48:3 *simul in unum* meets the row *in unum → juntos* and must decide locally**. Options *juntamente* (MS1932 in Ps 52), *ao mesmo tempo* |

| esca / cibus (*sicut escam panis*, *ut cibum panis*) | *como quem come pão* | open | Ps 13:4; 52:5 has *ut cibum panis* — one Greek (βρώσει ἄρτου) for both, so one Portuguese. The Latinist (Ps 13 draft 2, minor, having passed it on draft 1) read *esca* as the food and asked *como alimento de pão* — refused, option there. Elsewhere *esca* is food given (68:22, 103:21, 135:25 *Qui dat escam omni carni*, 144:15 …, 17 lines) and will be *alimento* or *comida* |

| captívitas | cativeiro | working | Ps 13:7 (= 52:7), 67:19a *cepísti captivitátem*, 77:61, 84:2, 125:1, 125:4 (grep). With *avértere* → *afastar o cativeiro* (13:7, 84:2); with *convértere* (52:7, 125:1, 125:4) the row *convértere* decides |

| *Quis dabit …?* | *Quem dará …?* | open | Ps 13:7 = 52:7 *Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël?* → *Quem dará de Sião a salvação de Israel?* — the question kept, which in Latin is also a wish; 54:7 *Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ* is the other place (grep). Heard as 'who will bring salvation from Sion'. Options *Quem enviará* (MS1932), *Oxalá venha* (DM1962's sense) |
formulas: | **Ps 13 / Ps 52, the doublet — what is shared word for word** (grep and side by side: `consult/parallels/ps013.md`, `ps052.md`; Clementine fetched `consult/bolls-VULG-19-13.json`, `-19-52.json`) | Ps 13 draft 2 wording, for Ps 52 to copy: **13:1a = 52:1** *Disse o insensato no seu coração: * Não há Deus.* · **13:3a = 52:4** *Todos se desviaram, juntos se tornaram inúteis: * não há quem faça o bem, não há nem sequer um.* · **13:5b = 52:6b** *ali tremeram de temor, onde não havia temor.* · **13:7a = 52:7a** *Quem dará de Sião a salvação de Israel?* · **13:7 end = 52:7 end** *… o cativeiro do seu povo, Jacó exultará, e Israel se alegrará.* **Shared in part:** 13:1b / 52:2 *Corromperam-se, e tornaram-se abomináveis … * não há quem faça o bem* (52: *nas suas iniquidades*, and no *não há nem sequer um*); 13:2 / 52:3 *Deus olhou do céu para os filhos dos homens, * para ver se há quem entenda, ou quem procure a Deus* (only Dóminus / Deus differ); 13:4 / 52:5 *Não hão de saber todos os que praticam a iniquidade, * os que devoram o meu povo como quem come pão?* (cognóscent / scient, sicut escam / ut cibum — one Greek each, so one Portuguese); 13:5a / 52:6a *Ao Senhor não invocaram* → *A Deus não invocaram*. **Not shared:** 13:3b–3d (not in Ps 52, nor in the Hebrew; in the Rahlfs LXX on disk and in Rom 3:13–18, fetched); 13:6 against 52:6b; *cum avérterit Dóminus* (→ *afastar*) against *cum convérterit Deus* (row *convértere*) | working — Ps 13; **Ps 52 copies** |

| *Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, † linguis suis dolóse agébant* (5:11a = 13:3b) + *venénum áspidum sub lábiis eórum* (13:3b's third colon; = Rom 3:13) | *… † com as suas línguas enganavam, * veneno de áspides debaixo dos seus lábios* | working — Ps 13 copied Ps 5's two colons exactly; the third left verbless as the Latin (the Latinist passed it twice) |
